source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Take the missed active pill as soon as possible and continue the remaining pills on schedule","B":"Discard the missed pill and take only the next scheduled pill at the usual daily time","C":"Discard the current package and begin a completely new package immediately after one miss","D":"Take two additional pills at the next scheduled time regardless of how late the pill is"}}
source_row.rationale: General guidance for a single missed combined oral contraceptive pill is to take the missed pill as soon as remembered (which may mean taking two pills in one day) and continue the rest of the pack as scheduled, though clients should always be directed to the specific product's labeling or consult their provider/pharmacist, since instructions can vary and backup contraception may be recommended depending on the number of missed pills and timing in the cycle.
source_row.source_detail: Late/missed combined oral contraceptive: take one late/missed active pill as soon as possible and continue remaining pills, even if two pills are taken the same day; 2024 U.S. SPR; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Combined Hormonal Contraceptives, U.S. SPR 2024
source_row.stem: A client taking a combined oral contraceptive asks the nurse what to do after missing one pill, mentioning a friend told her to just double up on the very next scheduled pill instead of taking the missed one separately. The nurse should generally advise the client to instead:
